userStories.title: Add -smoke=<category> flag to cmd/probe_chat for category-filtered re-runs
userStories.description: The 2026-05-18 Q&A skill v6 SMOKE TIER section (`references/dispatch-prompts.md` Phase 5 line ~543) says: 'Re-run a SMOKE TIER first: the failing case + all cases in the same subject category (same tool / channel / failure-mode family per qa-coverage-tools.md / qa-coverage-channel-failure.md), cap 8 cases. Random selection forbidden — select by infrastructure overlap with the fix.' But cmd/probe_chat/main.go currently only supports `-case=<exactname>` (single case) or no flag (all cases). There is no way to run a category subset. This story adds `-smoke=<category>` where category is one of: `tools-files`, `tools-memory`, `tools-source`, `tools-web`, `tools-scheduler`, `tools-agent-note`, `channels-telegram`, `channels-web`, `failure-modes-budget`, `failure-modes-phantom`, `markitdown`. The categorization comes from grouping cases.go entries by their primary subject. (a) Add a `caseCategory` field to the Case struct in cmd/probe_chat/types.go (or a parallel map[string][]string in cases.go keyed by category). (b) Add `-smoke string` flag in main.go that filters allCases() by category. (c) Document the categories in main.go usage comment block (lines 16-30) — list them inline so the LLM-readable code matches user behavior. (d) Test in three modes: `-smoke=markitdown` (should run only the 6 markitdown-* cases), `-smoke=channels-web` (cases tied to /api/chat web-bearer behavior), `-smoke=nonexistent` (should print error listing valid categories and exit non-zero). (e) Cap at 8 cases per category — if a category has more, take the first 8 alphabetically and emit a warning to stderr.

userStories.title: Decouple conversation_id from user_id at /api/chat (US-QA21 design smell fix)
userStories.description: Per docs/qa-bug-log.md (2026-05-18 triage of agent-note-roundtrip): `cmd/aura/web_chat.go:401` currently does `toolCtx = toolregistry.WithConversationID(toolCtx, e.userID)`, binding conversation_id to user_id. This collapses the agent_note tool's per-conversation scratchpad to one-note-per-user — violates the tool's docstring promise of per-conversation scoping (see internal/agent/tools/registry/agent_note.go line 14-17 with Get/Set/Append/Clear all taking conversationID). The triager filed this as US-QA21 / P2 design smell. This story implements the fix: (a) Read cmd/aura/web_chat.go around line 401 — understand the e struct + how userID is sourced. (b) Define what 'conversation' means for the web channel. Options: (i) Per-request — every /api/chat call is its own conversation (worst, loses memory). (ii) Per-thread — /api/chat accepts an optional thread_id parameter; if provided, conversation_id = `web:<thread_id>`; if absent, defaults to a session-scoped value derived from bearer (NOT user_id directly, but something like `web:<user_id>:default`). (iii) Per-bearer-token — each minted token = one conversation (clean but ties scratchpad lifecycle to token lifecycle). RECOMMENDED option (ii) with `web:<user_id>:<thread_id_or_default>` to preserve the existing default behavior while enabling explicit threading. (c) Add a `ThreadID` field to api.ChatRequest (optional string) and plumb it to e.userID context binding logic. (d) Backward-compat: requests without ThreadID get `web:<userID>:default` — same scratchpad as today but with a clearer namespacing. (e) Update cmd/probe_chat/cases.go agent-note-roundtrip Verify if needed — should still work because we kept the time-window query, but verify the stderr preview shows the new conversation_id format. (f) Add a regression test in internal/api/chat_test.go that sends 2 requests with different ThreadIDs and asserts agent_notes has 2 distinct rows.
acceptanceCriteria: api.ChatRequest has new optional ThreadID string field (json:'thread_id,omitempty')
cmd/aura/web_chat.go:401 (or nearby) sets conversation_id = `web:<userID>:<thread_id_or_default>` instead of just userID
Default thread_id is 'default' (or similar single keyword) — documented in struct field tag/comment
New test in internal/api/chat_test.go (or web_chat_test.go) sends 2 chat requests with thread_id='a' and thread_id='b' and asserts 2 rows in agent_notes with distinct conversation_id values
Existing chat_test.go tests still pass (backward compat for omitted thread_id)
cmd/probe_chat baseline: agent-note-roundtrip still passes (uses time-window query, robust to conversation_id format change)
Skill probe stderr preview now shows conversation_id starting with 'web:' prefix (visual confirmation of new format)
go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test ./... all green
Single atomic commit prefix: fix(api): decouple conversation_id from user_id in /api/chat (Phase-QA1 / US-QA-FIX03 / US-QA21)
userStories.notes: Don't go further than per-thread namespacing — full per-conversation isolation (option iii) would require API breaking changes. Option (ii) preserves backward compat: requests without thread_id continue to behave as today. The `web:` prefix in conversation_id is intentional — makes it grep-able for 'all web-channel notes' vs other channels (telegram, cron) which use different formats.

userStories.title: Rewrite phase07d/e probe Setup to seed via API instead of direct DB write
userStories.description: Per .planning/qa/baseline-run.json (2026-05-18 baseline), cmd/probe_chat case `phase07d-mixed-tier-recall` and `phase07e-source-span-read` both FAIL with transport_err: 'setup: probe_chat phase07{d,e} fixture would write data\\aura.db while the Docker Aura service is running; run inside Compose or stop it first with docker compose stop aura'. This is an INFRA test-pattern bug, not a product bug — the Setup function in cmd/probe_chat/phase07d.go (and phase07e.go) refuses to write seed data directly to data/aura.db when it detects Aura container is running (because concurrent writers would corrupt SQLite WAL). The right architectural fix: seed via Aura's own /api endpoints instead of direct DB write. (a) Read cmd/probe_chat/phase07d.go to identify exactly what fixtures are seeded (likely user-memory rows, operational-recall rows). (b) For each fixture, find the corresponding /api endpoint that writes them (e.g., /api/memory/user/set, /api/memory/operational/log) — search internal/api/router.go. If a matching endpoint exists, use it. If not, document the gap (skip this fixture and add a follow-up story). (c) Replace direct SQL writes with HTTP POSTs via env.APIClient. (d) Same for phase07e.go (likely source-span fixture — should use /api/sources POST instead). (e) Remove the 'container detected' guard from Setup, since API-driven seeding is concurrent-safe (Aura's own sqlite layer handles WAL). (f) Re-run probe_chat baseline: expect 21/21 PASS (or 20/21 with the 1 known FLAKE doc-pdf-roundtrip). (g) Update .planning/qa/baseline-run.json snapshot in docs/qa-verdict.md follow-ups if appropriate.

Full baseline (go run ./cmd/probe_chat -json) shows at least 20/21 PASS (the 1 acceptable miss is the doc-pdf FLAKE classified 2/4 in docs/qa-bug-log.md — not regression from this fix)

userStories.title: Stabilize doc-pdf-roundtrip flake — LLM mis-echoes hex source_id
userStories.description: Per docs/qa-bug-log.md (2026-05-18 flake protocol): cmd/probe_chat case `doc-pdf-roundtrip` flaked 2/4 across re-runs. Failure pattern: the LLM mistypes the 16-char hex source_id when echoing it in the reply — e.g., quotes 'src_89ceda2013a00d59' when actual is 'src_89ceda2013d00a59' (one digit off), or quotes a completely different hash (wholesale hallucination). The PDF is created + persisted correctly each run; the failure is exclusively in the LLM's echo. Per skill v6 flakiness protocol: 2/4 fail = FLAKE, don't propose a fix yet, investigate determinism. This story IS that investigation + fix. Two complementary fixes (do BOTH): (a) **Prompt hardening** — rewrite the case's Prompt field in cmd/probe_chat/cases.go to instruct the LLM 'echo the source_id verbatim, character-for-character, no transformation' with a concrete example like 'if source_id is src_abc123, reply src_abc123'. (b) **Assertion relaxation** — modify the Verify function to accept any reply that contains the source_id PREFIX (`src_` + first 8 hex chars) rather than requiring full match. Rationale: the storage path is what's actually being tested, not the model's ability to copy a 16-char hex string. If the prefix matches, the model called the right tool and got the right source. Verify both fixes by running `go run ./cmd/probe_chat -case=doc-pdf-roundtrip -json` 5 times in a row — must pass ≥4/5 (re-classified from FLAKE to acceptable per skill rule '4/4 fail = real bug; 3/4 = suspect; 2/4 = flake' — we're targeting 4/5+ = not-flake).
acceptanceCriteria: cmd/probe_chat/cases.go doc-pdf-roundtrip Prompt field includes explicit 'echo source_id verbatim' instruction with example

cmd/probe_chat/cases.go doc-pdf-roundtrip Verify accepts reply containing the source_id prefix (first 12 chars = 'src_' + 8 hex) rather than exact 16-char match — OR uses substring containment with the full id (whichever is cleaner)
5-run loop: `for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do go run ./cmd/probe_chat -case=doc-pdf-roundtrip -json > /tmp/pdf-run-$i.json; done` results in ≥4/5 pass:true (acceptable rate; 5/5 ideal)

Update docs/qa-bug-log.md entry for doc-pdf-roundtrip: status changes from 'flake-monitoring (FLAKE classification)' to 'fixed in <SHA> by prompt-hardening + assertion-relaxation, 4/5 or 5/5 pass post-fix'
go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test ./... green
Single atomic commit prefix: test(probe_chat): stabilize doc-pdf-roundtrip — verbatim source_id echo + prefix assertion (Phase-QA1 / US-QA-FIX05)
userStories.notes: Don't over-relax — if you accept arbitrary substring, the test loses signal. The prefix approach (src_ + 8 hex chars) is enough to distinguish: random 8 hex matches by accident in only 1/(16^8) ≈ 1 in 4 billion — sufficient probability bound for a test assertion. The full 16-char hex is overkill for a test that's really verifying 'did the right tool fire and produce the right artifact'.
